name: BSP_LoadingScreen_ReportProgress
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frontend_shell_entry, read-only analysis. __stdcall(float progress), RET 4, no ECX; a null 00E194B4 is a no-op (0057bec9). Raises screen+30h to max(screen+30h, progress) and screen+2Ch to max(screen+2Ch, LIBCRT 00bf7420 counter); neither is ever lowered (0057bf04 JG then 0057bf06 JZ). x87 checked on disk: 0057beef FMUL qword [00CEF258] (=128.0) leaves its product in ST0 and it is never stored, because 0057bef5 is an SSE MOVSS of the unscaled maximum; ST0 is also left loaded on return. Ghidra and the raw decoder agree, so the dead multiply and x87 stack leak are in the shipped code. Sole non-trivial caller 004e4000 at 004e413a with the 0.1f at 00D7A2F0. Evidence: docs/GAME_FRONTEND_ENTRY.md.

name: BSP_LoadingScreen_RegisterSingleton
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frontend_shell_entry, read-only analysis. __thiscall, ECX = the loading screen + 8h, RET 0, returns this in EAX. Constructor of the singleton-lifetime base: stores vtable 00CEF260, takes the lifetime manager's critical section at manager+10h with a nesting counter, assigns the global DAT_00E194B4 = this - 8 and registers the node through 00415350 and BSP_SingletonLifetime_Register, then leaves the section. Because the global is assigned inside this constructor rather than by the caller, 0057cb60 can read 00E194B4 immediately after 0057c1c0 returns without an explicit store. Sole caller 0057c1c0. Evidence: docs/GAME_FRONTEND_ENTRY.md.

name: BSP_LoadingScreen_Construct
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frontend_shell_entry, read-only analysis. __thiscall, RET 0, returns this in EAX. Constructor of the 0x58-byte loading screen at 00E194B4. Chains BSP_FrontEndScreen_Construct (004f7180, which stores vtable 00CEAE54 and clears the +4h wanted and +5h active bytes) and 0057bff0 on this+8h, then stores vtable 00CEF264 at +0h and 00CEF28C at +8h and sets +38h=0, +3Ch=0, +40h=1, +44h=0. The GUI element pointers at +1Ch..+28h and the progress fields at +2Ch/+30h are not set here; vtable +10h, which 0057cb60 calls immediately after, is the only candidate. Sole caller 0057cb60 at 0057ccae. Evidence: docs/GAME_FRONTEND_ENTRY.md.

name: BSP_LoadingScreen_End
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frontend_shell_entry, read-only analysis. __cdecl(void), RET 0. Refreshes the GUI (004c12b0 then 00aa2b80), resumes the session object at game+1EF0h (0076c230) when 00E188A8 is non-null, then, if 00E194B4 exists, calls vtable +1Ch when the +5h active byte is set, clears +4h and +5h, commits through 004f83b0, unregisters the lifetime node at screen+8h (00415350 then 00bcfca0) and destroys the screen through vtable +0Ch with 1 before nulling the global. Called on both exits of 004e4000 (004e4159 on the platform-event abort and 004e43e7 on success), so the loading screen never outlives the front-end entry. Evidence: docs/GAME_FRONTEND_ENTRY.md.

name: BSP_LoadingScreen_Begin
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frontend_shell_entry, read-only analysis. __fastcall(int mode) with ECX holding the mode, NOT a this pointer: 0057cb7a moves ECX to EBP and the body never dereferences it; 004e4000 passes 0 via XOR ECX,ECX at 004e4114. RET 0. Clears and presents both swap-chain buffers through 00F8D394 vtable +0Ch/+14h twice, suspends the session object at game+1EF0h (0076c190), disables the GUI (004c12b0 then 00aa0e00) and runs one +0.0f GUI update (00aa4f80), resets the screen pump (004f8ac0, ECX=00E18D48), tears down the screen at 00E19698, loads interface/textures/allbutingame.ats through 00af0060 (ECX=00F8C26C), then creates the 0x58-byte loading-screen singleton at 00E194B4 via operator new + 0057c1c0 and its vtable +10h. Mode 0 loads interface/textures/menu.ats and configures elements +1Ch..+28h; mode 1 binds the published image at 00E08790 through 00abaed0 and computes an aspect-corrected rect; any other value configures nothing. Ends by setting the +4h/+5h flag bytes, 004f83b0, vtable +18h, 00F8D394 vtable +1Ch and BSP_RenderMode_PrepareAndStartWorker(screen+0Ch, callback 0057ca00, context screen+10h, rate 19h), so the screen animates on a render worker while the caller blocks. Evidence: docs/GAME_FRONTEND_ENTRY.md.

name: BSP_LoadingScreen_PublishConfig
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frontend_shell_entry, read-only analysis. __thiscall, ECX = a loading-screen config object, RET 0. Copies it into the global block at 00E08780: the vector of image names at +4h..+0Ch through 00506c80 (ECX=00E08780), the NativeString at +10h/+14h into 00E08790/00E08794 through 0041dd40 plus memcpy, and the byte at +18h into 00E08798. Both the vector owner check inside 00506c80 and 0057d002 make publishing the globals onto themselves a no-op that still stores the byte. Sole caller 004e4000 at 004e4101, which passes the object 0057d0d0 just returned in EAX. Evidence: docs/GAME_FRONTEND_ENTRY.md.

name: BSP_LoadingScreen_BuildDefaultConfig
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frontend_shell_entry, read-only analysis. __thiscall, ECX = an uninitialised caller local of the loading-screen config layout, RET 0, returns this in EAX. Zeroes +4h..+14h and sets +18h=1, then appends three NativeStrings of length 0Dh through 00450540: mp.loading_24 (00CEF348), mp.loading_05 and mp.loading_12. Field +0h is never written on this path and is unidentified. At 0057d25a it copies the live global byte 00E08798 back into +18h, so the seeded 1 never reaches a caller and the previous load's visibility is preserved. Sole caller 004e4000 at 004e40f6; the temporary is destroyed at 004d2a80. Evidence: docs/GAME_FRONTEND_ENTRY.md.
